name: Double-Half-Wing Crossed-Subcube Obstructions
statement: Let $V\ne\varnothing$, take $U=\varnothing$ and $\alpha=\beta=1$ in the crossed construction, and additionally delete $\{a,b,p\}$. The base remains a learning space. For endpoints $R=\{b,p\}\cup V$ and $\bar R=\{a,q\}$, the repair sets are $\{a,q\}\cup V$ and $\{b,p\}$. The pendant extension is contraction-minimal nonlearning of order $2^d-3\cdot2^{|V|}-2$. If $V=\varnothing$, $R$ is valid, so the hypothesis is sharp.
proof: Hereditary deletion of the additional state preserves union closure and accessibility. Three explicit rooted-union witnesses give the first endpoint holes; the second wing remains the exact other hole set. The new hole preserves the first repair set, the second is unchanged, and together they cover $X$.
